They captured this employee manually on SAP, Hi Lynnell and Amorey,  We have investigated the issue and found that original cause of the issue is related to the use of the booking type "Manual Adjustment" in the Leave balance replication from SAP to EC, compared to using "Accrual". In the case of terminations, the leave balance for an terminated employee is only cleared from EC when the next Leave balance replication runs after the termination date which is at the soonest the day after the termination but in the case of backdated termination it could be many more days. The interface therefore clears the leave balances and post the clearing on the day when the interface ran after the termination had been recorded.  This "late" posting to the employees Time accounts in EC to clear the balance, causes and issue on the rehire of an employee due to the system not being able to adjust Time accounts. On rehire, the system attempts to shrink existing Time accounts to fall outside of the new rehire date so that a new Time account for the rehire may be created, however if there is a Manual adjustment in the way because of an balance replication then the system cannot correct the Time account.  We have tested in T1 using the Booking type "Accruals" instead of "Manual Adjustments", and found that the system is then able to adjust the Time account as necessary.  We initially opted to use "Manual Adjustments" because the Booking type "Accruals" is generally reserved for system generated accruals, and we wanted to distinguish between those updates made by the interface.  We therefore propose that the interface be changed to stop posting updates to Time accounts as "Manual Adjustments" but instead post as "Accruals". This is a relatively simple change on the interface, however testing by O&L is encouraged before the change is moved to PROD.Additionally, the existing records in the Time accounts need to be changed to have a Booking Type of "Accrual instead".  The issue only affects the Sick leave Time accounts, therefore the data change can be limited to these Time accounts however this can also be left as is and dealt with on a case by case basis. column13: In order to avoid data replication conflicts with backdated changes to Payment Information Details (IT0009 Bank Details) dated before a previous payroll run date, all payment information details are set to use the current payroll period start date as the effective date in SAP. column14: We have logged a SAP Incident around the issue: 145577/2020 EC to SAP Employee Replication - Start Date Based on Payroll Period Date, We believe that the best solution may be the least technical. We propose that checking the date of the Payment Information changes in EC be part of the internal process when approving workflows. If the payment information change is dated before the last payroll run (or if payroll is currently running), the date should be changed to be the first of the following month.  If there is an error on the bank details replication, the relevant HR/HRBP should be notified and requested to change the payment information details to start on the following month., This ticket is still with SAP. There is an issue with the R/3 Connection for SAP to get into the On-Premise SAP system.  Daymien is taking it up with the Network Team, and he has also logged a SAP ticket to check the network connectivity., Daymien has resolved the connection issues and I have updated the SAP ticket. SAP should be able to troubleshoot now., SAP have come back with the following recommendations:We can either change the Payment Information to replicate to Infotype 0009 to use the start date of the record in ECOr we should only have one Bank Details change in a Payroll MonthThe way that the replication is currently configured to use the Payroll Start Date as the Start Date of the Infotype 0009 record will not work if there are multiple changes in one Payroll month., Employees have access to change bank details, so limiting this to only 1 change per month (which ideally should be the case) is u fortunately not practically possible. column14: Thank you Marco, Hi Lynnell,  As mentioned before the root cause is with the configuration of the Position Management Settings and how it handles syncing of changes from the position to the employee. When you applied a change to the position 20000859, the system then kicked off the POSTOJOB rule which syncs any changes from the position to the employee. The manual changes that had been applied to the employee, the workschedule for example, was then overwritten with the data from the position.  Currently the SF cannot determine which differences on the employee's Job history is because of a change on the employee or because the employee has different details to that of the positions.  The proposed solutions is as follows:Simplify the POSTOJOB rule - we could create an additional rule for sync of info from the Position to Job History/Info in case of a update made to a position. This rule would have less fields listed and only those fields that should always be synced from the Position to Job History/Info. Then there will be a second rule on the employees Job History/Info which populates the values from the position in the case of when a position is selected or changed. Not recommended - as position and employee information will likely go out of sync due to changes made on the position that is not synced to the employee. LOE: no rule would need to be created. Testing would need to be done to confirm the config works in all scenarios. at least 8h.Enable the option to choose when to sync changes to incumbents - there is an option to request the changer to specify if the changes on a position need to be synced to the position or not. Not recommended - if the option is available there will be cases when users select not to sync the change to the employee, which would likely cause the employee information to go out of sync with the position. LOE: a config change needs to be made to the Position management settings to allow users to choose when a change is synced to the incumbents.New positions for differences - when an employee's data differs from that of the position, it is recommended that a new position be created for the employee with the updated date. It is also recommended that the fields on the Job information for an employee be made read-only to force users to create a new position when there are such differences. Without creating a new position when there are changes then there is no way to prevent system from overriding manual changes made to an employee. LOE: no new config is required.Kindly confirm which solution you would like to have implemented.  Kind regards, Marco Smith, Hi Amorey,  My apologies, I have spoken to Irene and reviewed the config and you are 100% correct the agreed upon process was as per the image. The 2 options to perform a LE transfer is as follows:Performing a Termination action using the Event "Termination", with an Event reason specific to the LE transfer. After which a rehire is done, which will update the Hire date to the new effective date of the event.Performing a Job Change, using the Event "Job Change" and the Event reason "Legal entity transfer". Provided this is accurate, please have an overview of the following current information:  Some Important Background Info:With the initial Data Migration; the methodology was followed where the Hire Date = Go-Live Date = 1st Job Information record.  The actual Hire Date of the employee is captured in the field Original Start Date in Employment InformationThe Hire Date field is not replicated into SAP OnPrem.  In EC, the Hire Date has actually no real value other than to indicate the 1st Job Info record.  In my opinion it can be hidden from the Employment Details section altogetherNow here is the real dilemma: The Hire Date can only be changed in EC in particular situations; of which the most obvious one is that the Hire Date should be in the past.  This is a built in EC check and it cannot be bypassed.  The Hire Date is used in Onboarding to trigger the Crossboarding process. Recommendation:  Given the problem statement and keeping in mind the function and restrictions around the Hire Date, I would recommend that it is solved as follows:  Configure a field in Employment Details that keeps track of:Original Hire date when Hire Event occurs, andUpdate only in the event of Legal Entity Transfer (or any event that will trigger a Crossboarding process)This can be done with Business RulesThis field can be hidden to users as it will only act as a technical field.  However, if this field will hold value, it can be displayed.The Onboarding module  will need configuration to pull this custom date into mapping to be able to trigger the Crossboarding notification on the correct date.This field will not replicate into SAP OnPrem.As a sidenote, since the Hire Date does not really add any value; I would recommend to hide it altogether. column13: Hourly employee master data replication stopped on 14 May at 19.30, all jobs still completed successfully on SAP but the Artifact was not triggered in CPI, manual individual replication was successfully but only on single employees. Once this was picked up we did some investigation and concluded that the variant HOURLY_REPL that is called when the job HOURLY_EMP_REPL runs could be the problem. I then edited the variant by adding =* in External Employee ID field. This triggered the Artifact in CPI when the job ran hourly, however I picked up that changes are not detected by the system so hourly replication basically does nothing. column12: Custom Field Required for Payment Method : PreNumbered Cheques
column13: Problem: Hangana payroll managers captured Prenumbered Cheque as a payment information type directly on SAP before payroll tax year close. Because of payroll tax year close we cannot remove the record in SAP as that would give a retro error. To enable replication from SF to SAP the records must correspond 100%. I have configured the visibility of fields necessary on SF, however on SAP there is a bank name with no bank key (sort code/routing number) if i create this bank on SF with no routing number the system gives the error "Incorrect Banking details" i have disabled the tick for banking verification in Company Logo Settings, but I still get this error. User affected = 50930  SAP Ticket 210809 / 2021 Disable Banking Verification Logged  Solution Suggested:  The Bank Validations switch in Company System and Logo Settings checks the country-specific format and deep validations for the fields: Account Number, Routing Number, IBAN, and BIC/SWIFT codeThis, however, does not disable the hardcoded validation for the Bank objectthere's no way for us to bypass this since this validation is in the Code level.  KBA:2519996 vwas suggested but it did not provide a valid solution   For you to proceed on maintaining "Bank" details without having this error, you can opt to use a Custom field/Custom Bank Object under PaymentInformationDetailv3 instead. This can serve as a place holder on list of available Banks in your system for the Prenumbered Cheque scenario like this.  It is also important to note that there needs to be some adjustments with your configuration for the integration with payroll (in order for the data to be replicated properly).

column14: Hi Lynnell I hope you are well I would like to take this opportunity to give an update on the Absenteeism report and formulate a way forward.  Background: Currently the Group Wellness Manager extracts a raw data report from SAP HCM which indicates the number of specified leave days taken for a specified period of time and the Planned working days. This information is pasted in an Excel Spread sheet and graphs are formulated according to report requirements. EPI-USE was instructed to create a Report on SF to extract all the necessary data from SF and that would be pasted in a template of pre-configure graphs which would then be updated upon refresh. Progress: I managed to extract the necessary data required for the specified leaved types, however encountered some challenges when it came to the Planned working Days. According to the information provided to me Planned Working days is define as: Basic / 21 Planned Working Days = Daily rate (5 Day worker) Basic / 26 Planned Working Days = Daily rate (6 Day worker)   The definition of planned work days as per input provided for the sustainability report in 2016 is:Planned work days are: 21.67 Planned work days per month for 5-day worker and 26.67 Planned work days per month for 6-day worker.   However, the results based on this formula and the results presented by the reports extracted from SAP did not correspond. After multiple meetings between myself, Giovanni and Jannie we managed to understand the formula used by SAP to calculate Planned Working Days as: Planned working days - Takes into account all employees who are or were in service during the specified period for employees who were active during the whole specified period = 20.83333333333333*12 (monthly planned days * 12)for employees who started during that period the starting date is taken into account = 20.83333333333333*2.5 (monthly planned days * months active - column13: Please see below where the Contract End date ‘lives’ in SAP. Can the contract end date added in EC not be mapped to this field? Previously you indicated that it cannot but I would like us to double check please.
column14: Contract End Date is only going to be filled if there is a Termination Record in EC that has replicated to SAP. This will reflect as an Action for the employee.  The Contract End Date in EC cannot be replicated to the SAP field IT0000-ENDDA.  It will be replicated once the employee has a Contract End Date Termination record in EC., Adriaan can you please explain why this cannot be mapped? Currently we fill contract end date in SAP on hire, even if a termination record has not been captured. , Hi Amorey,  The Action infotype in SAP contains the events occurring on an employee's employment. It has fields for both Start and End dates for the events (BEGDA and ENDDA respectively). Due to the nature of the infotype, there cannot be any breaks; the ENDDA of the record is the day before the BEGDA of the following record:   These actions are mapped directly to the events in EC and need to be 1:1 for replication to occur. This means that we cannot create new actions in SAP if there is no matching event in EC.  The process of hiring a fixed term employee in both SAP and EC allows you to enter the "Contract End Date", but the process simply creates the future dated termination in the system and does not actually store the date in a field in SAP. If any action occurs between the hire and the termination, the ENNDA of the last action before the termination action will always be the same "Contract End Date", which is not something we can control during the mappings.

column12: Difference Between Absence Days and Quota Deducted for Saturday Leave
column13: While checking the absence quota replication from SAP to EC we encountered a strange case where an employee who has a 5 hour work day on a Saturday has future dated leave over that Saturday, but the leave only shows as 1/2 a day against the quota and a full day against the "Absence days" field. In EC these days are counted as full days, meaning that until the day of leave is in the past, SAP will have more days available than EC. If the employee takes multiple weeks of leave at once, the issue is compounded, leading to a multiple day difference between the two systems:             Is this expected in SAP? If so, do we need to account for these 1/2 days in EC?
column14: SAP allows for a working day to be counted as 1/2 day for quota deduction, but this is not supported in EC. SAP Note https://launchpad.support.sap.com/#/notes/0002830980 says:Once the end date is different from the start date, the system automatically understands that the leave will last for the full day and there is no options of changing it.  If you believe that this would be an important enhancement for future releases, please refer to the KBA on how to submit enhancement requests This will only affect future dated leave and as soon as the leave is in the past, it will be corrected by the interface., Please see attached file.

This is expected behaviour for the system not to allow you to save unless there are any fields marked as required that have not been completed.     LW: 2. When you update your candidate profile (tertiary) and you select have not yet graduated, it does not allow you to save and gives you the below error. Proficiency levels are used in the Capabilities Portfolio and in the Growth Portfolio in SuccessFactors. The Growth Portfolio needs to be configured before you can use it, please see the below information. This is used where you are using attributes (Competencies and Skills) in SuccessFactors.  Capabilities Portfolio This is where you can view the proficiency levels for an employee's capabilities, which are associated with their Job Role. Capabilities can be assessed via a Performance Form. Each capability has a proficiency rating scale assigned to them that determines what their scores can be. Before you can use the portfolio, you’ll have to use the setup wizard in the Manage Center of Capabilities screen to setup the rating scale / proficiency levels. You can also add or edit proficiency levels for skills in families. You will also need to associate which performance forms will show the proficiency history. Once you complete the set up, you can select Capabilities Portfolio from the main navigation to look at your capabilities. You will notice that when capabilities are rated in the performance forms, they are updated here as well. You can also use the Capabilities Portfolio to:View the capabilities assigned to an employee (Jos Specific Competencies maintained in Job Profile Builder)View an employee's current and historical proficiency ratings (Provided on Competencr ratings of Performance or Growth Portifolio)Access the SAP SuccessFactors Opportunity Marketplace to find opportunities to increase an employee's capabilities (This is a separate licensed module that can also integrate and use proficiency levels)Example   Growth Portfolio This is where employees can view their skills and attributes based on their current Job Profile. the Growth Portfolio is a new feature on the drop-down menu selected from 'home' that displays all the skills, competencies, and other attributes the system knows about a person. This enhancement was introduced last year to allow employees to use the Growth Portfolio to:View their skills and attributes based on their current Job Profile, which is pre-populatedAdd or reject skills that are recommended by the system based on AI (requires configuration and has additional costs)Assign a proficiency level for every Skill & Attribute in the portfolioSet a "Passion" flag for Attributes vital to themExample of the Growth Portifollio    Note that the Talent Intelligence Hub will be where these attributes will be managed going forward and you need to start looking at migrating to the Talent Intelligence Hub in the future. As a result, we are updating the two infotypes manually when infotype 2 is updated by the replication process.  We will be able to provide a test document early next week.  Regards, Jesse., Hi.  The use of a report to achieve this implementation might seem unreasonable at best. The below notes will try explaining why this was the chosen option.  We tried including infotypes 9745 and 9744 in the BIB configuration under Transformation Template Group T2_EMP_REPLICATION and Transformation Template NATIONAL ID, which maps to EC entity WS_17(PerNationalId). This was similar to the national id configuration but this proved impossible as BIB required infotypes with a decoupled framework.   At this point, we were sure that the only way is to perform the replication manually using SAP's HR operations. This approach would involve some code, leading us to consider where to place this code:  BAdi enhancement Z_EMPL_REPL_ENH_PERS_SUBAREA: We attempted to execute the code when processing infotype 0002, as it's called for EC entity PerNationalId. However, this resulted in a dump with error CX_HRPA_VOILATED_PRECONDITION whenever the function module HR_INFOTYPE_OPERATION was called to edit custom infotype data. Using separate class methods and function modules led to the same issue as the BAdi enhancement. It was therefore never moved to PROD as I first wanted to confirm why a line manager change also creates duplicate entries on an employee's job history and had to log a ticket with SAP. We've now also received feedback from SAP. Please find attached their response as well.  SAP insists that the system is doing so by design and that this is expected behaviour. As mentioned in SAPs feedback, "the hierarchy adaption is not handled by the sync rule, but by the hierarchy adaption tab in the position management settings tool. It is a separate sync of all the other fields that are being synced by the rule in the synchronization tab. So if you make a change in the position and this change includes changes to the leading hierarchy/manager; you can indeed get 2 entrees in the job history of the employee."  What SAP also recommends to do is to create a separate Event Reason for the event where a manager is changed: "What makes it somewhat confusing for you is that you are using the exact same event reason for both changes. You are using the event "data change" for both the rule sync and the hierarchy adaption. I would recommend to change or create another event specifically for manager change (you can even call this event "manager change" and set this event instead in the hierarchy adaption tab in the position management tool. After this you can still get 2 entrees in job info, but one of the events will be manager change and one will be data change."  So, 2 points to consider in light of the above-mentioned:  The business rule that I had to amend indeed works except for a manager change on position. Duplicates are not created on Job History otherwise.With the line manager change scenario, I would recommend to follow SAPs proposal in creating a separate Event Reason to test with. If you would want to keep the event reason as it's currently set up, there is nothing we can do further as SAP states that the above mentioned is by design and is expected behaviour.Please let me know if I can continue to test with a separate event reason for manager change so that I can update you with the feedback. Sincerely, The EPI-USE AMS Team  , Hi Desiree  The Latest People Profile uses specific "Smart Hiding" logic that differs from the legacy profile. This means it is a data-driven visibility requirement rather than a standard permission bug. The visibility of the Contact Information card is directly tied to the presence of both Email Information and Phone Information permissions and data. The user did not have an email address and if a user is missing a specific piece of data, the system may treat that entire section as null. If a user has no email address maintained, and you have configured the isPrimary flag as Mandatory, which you have, the system effectively sees an incomplete record. Because phone and email are grouped on the same card, a critical data gap in one (like a missing primary email) can cause the entire card to fail to render for that user.  To fix this I imported an email address for the user dummy@ol.na as well as their phone number info. This provided the system with the "Primary" flag it was looking for. This forced the Latest People Profile to recognize the user as having valid contact data, which "unlocked" the card's visibility. I then deleted the email address info, why this worked is because the initial import successfully refreshed the user's metadata and index for that card. Once the system "learned" that the card should be active for that user, it remained rendered even if the data was later cleared.  Since there are a number of employees without email addresses, you may want to reconsider if the isPrimary field should remain "Mandatory".  Kind Regards Yolanca, Hi Yolanca,   Noted with thanks. Will do the import.   Kind Regards,, Hi Yolanca,  It just defaults it back to Yes.    Kind regards,, Hi Desiree  Yes the isPrimary field is hard-coded at the system level to be mandatory for Email, Phone, and Emergency Contact Information, you can try and create a Defaulting rule. The current work around would be to import for all users that do not have email addresses. Do you require assistance with this?

Meaning when you make a field available for use with groups, by default it will be available to all users anywhere you have it in use. You would not want to use any field that is restricted to only certain roles.  The group membership will show all the users matching the criteria defined even if you don't have permission to view that field for all the users. For example, if you use Pay Scale Group and you can only view the Pay Scale Group of users in ND, and you create a group with the criteria of all the users with Pay Scale Group "B5 (NAM/PR/02/B5)", all the users with Pay Scale Group as "B5 (NAM/PR/02/B5)" will be shown in the group membership, not only the ones from ND. column14: Hi Desiree  In the Latest People Profile experience, header configuration has moved entirely to the Admin Center. While the legacy People Profile required Provisioning enablement, the new experience manages header fields through a revamped admin.  The display of Job Title and Department in the header is hard-coded by default. These fields are automatically pulled from the Employee Profile Title and Department fields, which are typically synchronized from EC Job Info via HRIS Sync. Because they are hard-coded for the standard view, you cannot simply deselect them in "Configure Latest People Profile" if you are not using an alternative differentiator.  To remove or replace these specific auto-populated fields, you must use an Employment Differentiator.
